_comment: Template for MCQ questions. Fill in 'subject', 'subject_key', and set 'id' starting values. Pass this to an AI alongside course content and PREPROMPT.md. Remove all _comment fields from the final output.
subject: [SUBJECT NAME]

questions._comment_type: mcq = 4-choice, truefalse = True/False only, code = 4-choice with a code snippet
questions._comment_difficulty: easy ~30%, medium ~50%, hard ~20% of total questions
questions._comment_distribution: Spread correct answers evenly: ~25% A, ~25% B, ~25% C, ~25% D across ALL mcq/code questions
questions._comment_choices: Always 4 choices labeled A–D. Each choice text must be a complete answer. Never use 'None of the above' or 'All of the above'
questions._comment_code: Optional. Raw code string, use \n for newlines. Only for type=code questions. Escape < as \x3C inside string values.
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of [concept X]?
questions.explanation: B is correct because [reason]. A is wrong because [reason]. C and D are wrong because [reason].

questions.question: [Statement that is either true or false about the subject].
questions.explanation: This is false because [reason]. The actual behavior is [clarification].

questions.question: What does the following code output?
questions.code:
# Replace with a code snippet in the target language
x = [1, 2, 3]
print(len(x))
questions.explanation: len() returns the number of elements. The list has 3 elements, so the output is 3. A and B are common off-by-one mistakes.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes [advanced concept Y]?
choices: B. Another plausible but incorrect description
C. A common misconception about Y
D. Correct and precise description of Y
questions.explanation: D is correct because [detailed reason]. A confuses Y with [related concept]. B describes [different concept]. C is a common misconception because [reason].
